labware.title: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is a flat plate, and Cloning needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is Cloning, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 2, load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the reaction can never be run. The plate map checks what each well holds, not what plate it is.
labware.fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

protocol.py: 4 biology problems (3 errors, 1 warning).

1. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well B1 in slot 1: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 48:  p20.aspirate(2, source_plate["B1"])
   At line 48 the p20_single_gen2 draws 2 ul from buffer (well B1 in slot 1) with its tip 1
   mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 24 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well
   Plate 200 µL Flat reaches only 0.75 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air
   (this line did it 12 times; 24 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does
   not follow the liquid. These are mixing strokes: the tip stirs air, and the well is not
   mixed.
   Affected: well B1 in slot 1.
   Fix: Mix lower, with `well.bottom(0.5)`, so the tip is in the liquid. This well needs
   about 35 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf

           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592

4. WARNING COLD-MODULE-NEVER-SET: A temperature module was loaded but never set

   At line 48 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 7 more in slot
   1, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at
   room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), enzyme
   (reagent), plasmid 1 (sample), plasmid 10 (sample) and 11 more sat on a block that was
   never cold; the robot pipetted there 48 times over the run. The person setting up the
   deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8
   and 7 more in slot 1.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 7 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from NEST 96 Well
   Plate 200 µL Flat in slot 1, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at the end.
   Source: Opentrons, temperature module: at room temperature until set_temperature, which
   blocks
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/temperature_module.html
   Source: Thermo Fisher T4 ligase manual: keep on ice, use within minutes

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: The pipette draws air from well B1 in slot 1: the liquid is below the tip
findings.explanation: At line 48 the p20_single_gen2 draws 2 ul from buffer (well B1 in slot 1) with its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 24 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat reaches only 0.75 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it 12 times; 24 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. These are mixing strokes: the tip stirs air, and the well is not mixed.
findings.fix: Mix lower, with `well.bottom(0.5)`, so the tip is in the liquid. This well needs about 35 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm.

By then the well holds 12 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat reaches only 0.38 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it 12 times; 12 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. These are mixing strokes: the tip stirs air, and the well is not mixed.

findings.title: A temperature module was loaded but never set
findings.explanation: At line 48 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 7 more in slot 1, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), enzyme (reagent), plasmid 1 (sample), plasmid 10 (sample) and 11 more sat on a block that was never cold; the robot pipetted there 48 times over the run. The person setting up the deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 7 more in slot 1.
findings.fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat in slot 1, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at the end.
